annotations.title: Find a chip's mainline Linux driver by name

description: Find whether mainline Linux has a driver for a chip, by NAME: give a part number or ordering code (for example 'MAX98357AETE+T', 'BME280', 'RTL8211F'). Returns the device-tree compatibles, I2C/SPI id-table names and Ethernet PHY driver names that match, each with how it matched (exact; the query is the longer ordering code; a wildcard family name such as 'sht3x'; a longer variant; a board driver that mentions it), the driver source files and the binding documents, for ONE kernel version stated in the answer. status is driver_found only for an exact or ordering-code match that has a driver file; a wildcard family or sibling is related_driver_found and must be confirmed in the binding document. not_found_by_name does NOT mean no driver exists: chips bound by USB, PCI or SDIO hardware ID, vendor kernels and out-of-tree drivers are not in the index; similar_names lists leads (a TCA9548A is driven as pca9548). It does NOT say whether your operating system's kernel is configured to build the driver. Free with a DatasheetVend API key (no credits), no model call, no network at call time, reads no account data.

limit.description: Most matches to return, strongest first. Default 10.

part.description: Part number or ordering code, for example 'MAX98357AETE+T'. At least 4 letters or digits.
